# tiny-cors

RFC-compliant CORS middleware for WSGI and ASGI. Zero dependencies. Single file.

## Run

```bash
pip install tiny-cors
```

## API

- `CorsConfig(...)` — dataclass. Fields: `allow_origins` (frozenset),
  `deny_origins` (frozenset), `allow_methods` (frozenset),
  `allow_headers` (frozenset), `expose_headers` (frozenset), `max_age`
  (int), `allow_credentials` (bool), `vary_origin` (bool),
  `allow_origin_func` (optional callable).
  - `is_origin_allowed(origin)` / `get_allowed_origin(origin)`
- `cors_middleware(config, app=None)` — WSGI middleware factory.
- `CorsMiddleware(app, config)` — WSGI class form.
- `ASGICorsMiddleware(app, config)` — ASGI class form.
- `PreflightCache(max_age=..., max_entries=...)` — caches preflight
  responses so repeated OPTIONS requests do not hit the app.
- `tiny_router_middleware(config)` — adapter for
  https://github.com/hussain-alsaibai/tiny-router apps.

## Usage

```python
from tiny_cors import CorsConfig, cors_middleware

config = CorsConfig(allow_origins=frozenset({"https://app.example.com"}))
app = cors_middleware(config, my_wsgi_app)
```

## Notes

- Handles preflight (OPTIONS) separately from the actual request.
- `Vary: Origin` is emitted whenever the response depends on the origin
  (`vary_origin=True` by default).
- With a wildcard origin and `allow_credentials=False` the response sends
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; with credentials on, the concrete
  origin is echoed instead, per the Fetch spec.
- `allow_origin_func` accepts a callable for dynamic origin decisions.

## Links

- Source: https://github.com/hussain-alsaibai/tiny-cors
- Part of the OpenClaw zero-dependency tiny-* ecosystem.
